title: SSP-3 — Resolver Tokens Delivery
summary: deliver context-aware current references with a fixed token inserted through the TE-1 Source Directives menu
content_html:
SSP-3 — Resolver Tokens Delivery

Status And Purpose

Proposed as SSP-3 after SSP-2 independently publishes the versioned Project State folder lookup. The completed SSP-1 foundation supplies normalized optional authoring subjects. Resolver Tokens Architecture owns the resolver, semantic-link, derived-usage, access, lifecycle, and non-goal contracts implemented by this delivery.

TE-1 — Directive Insertion provides the Source-toolbar Directives menu and guarded source-text insertion entry point used by SSP-3.2. SSP-3 contributes one later code-owned Insert current references snippet. TE-1 does not decide whether the containing collection or subject can resolve it; SSP-3's build consumer owns that fast, clean validation. The resolver core in SSP-3.0–3.1 does not depend on TE-1.

SSP-3 delivers the smallest reusable Resolver Token seam together with one complete context-aware current-references consumer.

Accepted SSP-1 Input

The containing document supplies one normalized SSP-1 object with exact state, kind, key, and fields, plus evidence only for malformed/conflicting state. Valid Folder context is available only in a collection whose registered assignable group gives folder_path meaning. Valid Work and Series context is collection-independent and carries the exact canonical scalar key. None and invalid states remain explicit unresolved inputs.

Resolver authoring inserts only the fixed subject-free token. The build consumer obtains normalized state from the registered containing-document source context. Folder dispatch reads one SSP-2 lookup row; Work or Series dispatch uses the exact key through Semantic Tokens. SSP-1's private subject-associations.json remains a document-association product, while rendered resolver output uses its focused lookup and semantic-link owners.

Complete Outcome

A managed document can contain one fixed Resolver Token carrying no resolver seed, subject kind, or subject key. At build time SSP-1's normalized metadata supplies the containing document's optional subject, its subject kind selects the code-owned resolver adapter, and the adapter performs one exact focused lookup or semantic-target read before rendering deterministic groups without mutating source or scanning live relationship owners.

For a folder context, those groups include Work[], Series[], and Project documents from the exact Project State row. A valid work_id or series_id in any collection resolves that exact declared identity through the existing Semantic Tokens target projection without Series roll-up or member-Work fan-out. Every returned Work or Series uses its semantic identity and the shared Semantic Tokens target/link projection. Each successful catalogue link creates one resolver-derived semantic usage row tied to the containing Resolver Token source range. Project-document results retain exact Docs Viewer target identity. Missing subject, empty, unavailable, stale, invalid, and denied states remain explicit and bounded.

Delivery Discipline

SSP-3 remains a bounded lookup consumer: a small resolver-definition registry, exact context-aware token parser, one-row relationship reader, declared-group renderer, bounded semantic-link projector, derived usage projection, and one predefined TE-1 Source-menu snippet. It must not become a graph database, query language, registry scanner, recursive traversal engine, live relationship service, or generic Source-command plugin system.

SSP-3.0 is a short scope-and-spec sanity gate over the builder, registered-context, Semantic Tokens, focused-lookup, and Source insertion boundaries. It confirms broad owners, blast radius, deliverables, risks, and stop conditions without freezing exact files, fixtures, estimates, or implementation. Each implementation stage ends with focused evidence and an independent code/diff review. If the generic core grows beyond what the specified contextual consumers require, pause for review and defer the abstraction until another proven consumer needs it.

Delivery Steps

SSP-3.0 — Confirm Scope And Delivery

  • [ ] Sanity-check the subject-free Resolver Token outcome against the accepted SSP-1 optional authoring-subject projection, SSP-2 folder lookup, current Markdown build, Semantic Tokens projection/usage, containing-document context, and TE-1 Directives insertion seam; resolve only contradictions that would change the result.
  • [ ] Confirm the broad blast radius across exact token recognition, registered context dispatch, one-row lookup, declared-group rendering, semantic-link projection, resolver-derived usage, targeted-build preservation, access isolation, and one code-owned Source convenience.
  • [ ] Confirm the deliverables: fixed subject-free token, bounded resolver definition/adapter seam, Project and Works result groups, exact Work/Series semantic usage evidence, inert failure states, focused verification, and concise durable owner updates.
  • [ ] Stop for review if the result requires recursive traversal, live relationship refresh, a graph/query system, a generic Source-command registry, or a broader abstraction than the specified contextual consumers need. Do not produce an exact file inventory, line estimate, frozen implementation, fixture implementation, or complete test architecture at this gate.

Checkpoint: a concise sanity note confirms the spec, scheduling dependencies, broad owners, blast radius, deliverables, risks, access boundary, and stop condition. Stop before implementation approval.

SSP-3.1 — Implement Resolver Core With Folder And Catalogue Adapters

  • [ ] Add the strict code-owned definition registry and schema/version checks.
  • [ ] Add the builder parser, registered containing-context dispatch, and one-lookup resolver interface.
  • [ ] Register the folder resolver against the SSP-2 generated lookup and the catalogue resolver against the normalized exact work_id/series_id plus existing Semantic Tokens target projection; add only other adapters whose focused products have accepted contracts.
  • [ ] Render accessible deterministic Work, Series, and Project-document groups plus explicit empty/error states without mutating source or crossing collection boundaries.
  • [ ] Route every Work and Series result through the existing semantic target lookup and link projector; emit no resolver-owned catalogue URL or fabricated Semantic Token source text.
  • [ ] Extend the generated semantic usage index and report with resolver-derived Work/Series occurrences tied to the containing Resolver Token range while preserving untouched documents during targeted builds.
  • [ ] Keep lookup paths, local folder targets, and service capabilities out of public build/runtime data.

Checkpoint: focused parser, context-dispatch, one-row lookup, rendering, semantic-link, derived-usage, targeted-build, stale/unavailable, and public-isolation evidence passes. An independent code/diff review confirms the core reads one focused lookup row, routes returned identities through shared Semantic Tokens projection, preserves authored source bytes, and leaves authoring workflow with SSP-3.2. Stop before SSP-3.2.

SSP-3.2 — Add Authoring Workflow

  • [ ] Contribute one code-owned Insert current references predefined snippet to the TE-1 Directives menu wherever that Source menu is available.
  • [ ] Insert the specified subject-free token through TE-1's captured-revision, guarded setRangeText, ordinary input/dirty-state, focus-return, and no-success-message workflow.
  • [ ] Reuse TE-1's frozen insertion-point behavior without adding Resolver-specific blank-line, collection, subject, lookup, or result eligibility checks, opening a subject picker, or previewing relationship groups.
  • [ ] Do not read or serialize folder_path, work_id, series_id, resolver ID, selected row, displayed URL, rendered document, or other UI context during insertion. Build-time registered document context is the only subject source.
  • [ ] Keep the existing TE-1 table-detail item and the Resolver snippet as predefined source conveniences; this bounded code-owned composition does not create a generic directive/plugin registry.
  • [ ] Make the dedicated build consumer recognise the exact token, resolve registered context, and fail quickly and cleanly to the specified inert/unresolved state for malformed, misplaced, unsupported, missing-subject, or unavailable cases.

Checkpoint: focused insertion-plan, stale-revision, dirty/focus, menu lifecycle, exact-token, clean-failure, and route-composition evidence passes. An independent code/diff review confirms the Source contribution reuses the existing owner, the build-time registered document context remains the subject authority, and the two bounded actions remain code-owned definitions. Stop before SSP-3.3.

SSP-3.3 — Verify And Transfer

  • [ ] Run focused parser, registry/lookup agreement, builder, rendering, authoring, semantic-link projection, derived usage indexing/reporting, targeted-build preservation, stale/unavailable, access-isolation, lint, and whitespace checks.
  • [ ] Prove the TE-1 menu item inserts the exact predefined bytes with the same keyboard, Escape/outside-click, route cleanup, stale-revision rejection, dirty-state, and focus-return behavior as the existing table-detail item, without invoking resolver validation.
  • [ ] Manually review realistic Project Work/Series/document groups, exact Work/Series subjects in different collections, no-subject state, long labels, and stale data at representative laptop/desktop widths.
  • [ ] Prove building a token-bearing document performs no filesystem, manifest, canonical Works, or canonical Series scan and does not refresh Project State.
  • [ ] Perform the independent final code/delivery review, reconcile completion claims with exact evidence and omissions, and record any bounded follow-up trigger.
  • [ ] Document the shipped generic resolver seam in a durable Docs Viewer architecture owner and update Semantic Tokens architecture/report contracts for resolver-derived usage; retain Project-specific result meaning in Project State.

Completion Evidence

  • One subject-free token in a folder-context document produces only the precomputed Work[] + Series[] + Project documents[] groups; copying that same source into another registered context intentionally changes its results.
  • A catalogue-subject token in any registered collection resolves only its exact declared work_id or series_id; collection identity and catalogue membership do not silently broaden the association.
  • Every returned Work or Series uses its semantic identity and the shared semantic-link projection, never a plain URL owned by the Project or Works lookup.
  • Every resolver-generated Work/Series link creates one derived usage row tied to its containing Resolver Token range, and the Semantic Tokens report can distinguish its origin and open the owning document at that location.
  • Maintained examples prove that a manual catalogue URL, authored Work/Series Semantic Token, and Resolver-generated semantic link can present the same destination while retaining different source and usage contracts.
  • Resolver-derived usage rows never fabricate Semantic Token source syntax. An unavailable Work or Series target produces neither a link nor a resolved usage row and does not fall back to an unvalidated URL.
  • Instrumented tests prove no build-time scan or chained relationship resolution; semantic projection is bounded to exact returned Work/Series identities.
  • Source remains byte-stable across successful, empty, stale, and unavailable expansion.
  • Authoring inserts one fixed token through the TE-1 Directives menu and never asks for, infers, previews, validates, or serializes a subject; the dedicated build consumer owns recognition and clean failure.
  • Public builds and runtime remain free of the Manage-only folder resolver definition, Project State lookup, local paths, and rendered local results.

Not In Scope

SSP-3 does not add recursive traversal, adjustable depth, relationship chaining, graph visualization, a global relationship database, automatic dependent-document rebuilds, public Project relationships, Semantic-to-Resolver Token migration, table-directive recognition, or a generic Source-command registry. Resolver Tokens Architecture owns the durable boundary.

Sub-Scope Publishing owns the flat SSP sequence. TE-1 owns the shared UI entry point and guarded Source edit; Resolver Tokens Architecture owns resolver-specific contracts, Project State Concept And Architecture owns Project lookup meaning, and Semantic Tokens Architecture owns semantic target projection and usage evidence.
